## IT & Web Tools

Hashes, encoders, cron, JWT, colours, networks and web snippets. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/it-web-tools/

- [File Checksum Generator (SHA-256, MD5, SHA-1)](https://ohfis.com/en/file-hash-generator/): Calculate and compare file hashes in your browser to verify downloads.
  Download pages publish a checksum so you can check that the file is exactly what the publisher built. Drop the file here, paste the published value and you immediately see whether they match. SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-1 and MD5 can be calculated at once, for files or for typed text.
  How to use: Drop a file (or type text) and choose the algorithms. Optionally paste the checksum from the download page into the compare field. Read the green or red result and copy the hash you need.
- [Subnet Calculator (CIDR, Netmask, IP Range)](https://ohfis.com/en/subnet-calculator/): Network, broadcast, usable hosts and subnet splitting for any IPv4 range.
  Enter 192.168.1.10/24 or an address with a mask such as 10.1.2.3 255.255.0.0 and see the network and broadcast address, the first and last usable host, the number of hosts, the wildcard mask, the binary mask, the address class and whether the range is private, loopback or public. Optionally split the network into equal smaller subnets.
  How to use: Enter an address with a prefix (/24) or a subnet mask. Read the network details. Optionally enter a longer prefix to split the network.
- [Cron Expression Translator](https://ohfis.com/en/cron-expression-translator/): Translate cron schedules into plain English and see the next run times.
  What does "30 4 1,15 * 5" do? Paste a crontab schedule and read it in plain English, then check the next dates it will run. Presets cover common schedules such as every 5 minutes, weekdays at 9:00 or the first of every month.
  How to use: Type or pick a cron expression. Read the plain-English description. Check the list of upcoming runs, in UTC or local time.
- [HTTP Status Codes Reference](https://ohfis.com/en/http-status-codes/): Search every HTTP status code with a plain explanation and a fix.
  Search by number or keyword to see what a status code means and what to do about it. All codes from 1xx to 5xx in the IANA registry that matter in practice are listed, grouped by class, each with a short explanation and a hint for fixing it.
  How to use: Type a code (404) or a keyword (redirect, timeout). Optionally filter by class. Read the explanation and what to try.
- [cURL to JavaScript & Python Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/curl-converter/): Turn a curl command into working fetch and Python requests code.
  API docs and browser dev tools give you curl commands. Paste one and get equivalent JavaScript fetch code and Python requests code with the same method, headers, body, basic auth and form fields.
  How to use: Paste a curl command (in the browser: Network tab → right-click a request → Copy as cURL). Read the generated JavaScript and Python. Copy the code you need.
- [User-Agent String Decoder](https://ohfis.com/en/user-agent-decoder/): Find out browser, OS, device and engine from a user-agent string.
  Paste a user-agent string from a log file or support ticket and see the browser and version, operating system, device type, rendering engine and whether it is a bot. Your own user agent is prefilled.
  How to use: Paste a user-agent string (or use yours). Read the decoded browser, system and device. Treat bot results with care: strings can be faked.
- [HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder](https://ohfis.com/en/html-entity-encoder/): Convert special characters to HTML entities and back.
  Show "<b>" as text on a web page, escape user input or decode &amp;eacute; in scraped text. Choose whether to escape only the five characters that matter in HTML (& < > " ') or also every non-ASCII character, as named entities (&eacute;) or as decimal or hexadecimal numbers (&#233;, &#xE9;).
  How to use: Choose encode or decode. Pick how much to escape. Paste your text and copy the result.
- [Base64 Encoder & Decoder (Text and Files)](https://ohfis.com/en/base64-encoder/): Encode or decode Base64 and data URLs, for text and for files.
  Convert text to Base64 or back, or encode any file by dropping it on the page. The tool detects whether your input looks like Base64 and decodes it automatically, recognises binary results such as images and PDFs and lets you download them, and supports the URL-safe alphabet used in JWTs and web links.
  How to use: Type text, paste Base64, or choose a file. Pick URL-safe, padding and line-length options if needed. Copy the result or download the decoded file.
- [Color Converter (HEX, RGB, HSL, CMYK)](https://ohfis.com/en/color-converter/): Convert colours between HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK, with picker and eyedropper.
  Type a colour in any common notation (#2557D6, rgb(37 87 214), hsl(223 70% 48%), cmyk(83 59 0 16) or a name such as coral) and get all the others, ready to copy. Use the picker or, in Chrome and Edge, the eyedropper to sample a colour from anywhere on your screen.
  How to use: Enter a colour or use the picker or eyedropper. Read all formats. Copy the one you need.
- [UUID / GUID Generator (v4 & v7)](https://ohfis.com/en/uuid-generator/): Generate batches of secure random UUIDs, including time-sortable v7.
  Create one UUID or ten thousand: version 4 (random) for general use, or version 7, which starts with a timestamp so IDs sort by creation time and keep database indexes fast. Output formats include upper case, without hyphens, Microsoft braces and SQL-quoted lists.
  How to use: Choose version, quantity and format. Change a setting or press "Generate new batch". Copy the list.
- [Number Base Converter (Binary, Octal, Decimal, Hex)](https://ohfis.com/en/number-base-converter/): Convert integers between bases 2 to 36, with arbitrary size.
  Enter a number in any base from 2 to 36 and see it in binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal and one more base of your choice. Prefixes such as 0x and 0b and underscores are understood, and numbers can be of any size, because the tool uses arbitrary-precision integers instead of floating point.
  How to use: Enter the number and choose its base. Read the other bases. Copy the value you need.
- [Basic Auth Header Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/basic-auth-header-generator/): Create the Authorization: Basic header from a username and password.
  Enter a username and password and get the exact HTTP header, plus the equivalent curl option. Useful for testing APIs, configuring webhooks or setting up a reverse proxy.
  How to use: Enter username and password. Copy the header or the curl option. Use it over HTTPS only.
- [Hex Color Alpha (Opacity to Hex) Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/hex-alpha-calculator/): Convert opacity percentages to two-digit hex alpha values like 50% = 80.
  Add transparency to a hex colour: enter the opacity in percent, get the two-digit suffix and, with a base colour, the complete 8-digit code (#2557D680). A table lists the usual steps from 0 to 100 percent.
  How to use: Enter the opacity in percent. Optionally enter the base colour. Copy the suffix or the complete colour.
- [Meta Viewport Tag Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/meta-viewport-generator/): Build a correct viewport tag for responsive pages.
  The viewport meta tag tells mobile browsers to use the device width instead of pretending to be a 980-pixel desktop. Choose the options and copy the tag; the generator keeps pinch-zoom enabled because disabling it fails accessibility requirements.
  How to use: Choose the width and initial scale. Add viewport-fit if you design for notched phones. Copy the tag into your <head>.
- [Favicon HTML Tag Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/favicon-html-generator/): Generate the link tags and manifest for desktop and mobile icons.
  Choose which icon files you have and get the right <link> tags, in the order browsers prefer, plus a ready web app manifest. Pair it with the Favicon & App Icon Generator to create the image files themselves.
  How to use: Enter the folder that holds your icons. Tick the icons you provide and set the theme colour. Copy the tags into <head> and save the manifest.
- [URL Query String Builder](https://ohfis.com/en/query-string-builder/): Turn key-value pairs into a correctly percent-encoded URL query string.
  List parameters as key=value lines and get the encoded query string, optionally appended to a base URL. Spaces, ampersands, equals signs, accents and emoji are escaped correctly, and repeated keys can be written as tag=a&tag=b, tag[]=a&tag[]=b or tag=a,b.
  How to use: Enter parameters as key=value lines. Choose how spaces and repeated keys are written. Copy the query string or the full URL.
- [Cache Buster URL Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/cache-buster-url-generator/): Append a version or timestamp parameter so browsers fetch the latest file.
  When you update a stylesheet or script and browsers or a CDN keep serving the old copy, a changed query string forces a fresh download. Paste the URLs, choose a timestamp, random string or fixed version and copy the busted URLs.
  How to use: Paste the URLs, one per line. Choose the parameter name and value type. Copy the new URLs.
- [SSL Certificate Expiry Checker & Reminder](https://ohfis.com/en/ssl-certificate-expiry-checker/): Read a certificate, see how many days remain and download calendar reminders.
  Expired certificates take websites down. Paste a certificate (PEM) and the tool reads who it was issued to and by whom, the alternative names, the signature algorithm and the validity dates, and tells you how many days are left. A download adds reminders 30, 14 and 7 days before expiry to your calendar. If you only know the date, enter that instead.
  How to use: Paste the certificate, or enter the expiry date. Read the days remaining and the details. Download the reminders for your calendar.
- [Email Header Analyzer](https://ohfis.com/en/email-header-analyzer/): Trace an email's route, delays and SPF, DKIM and DMARC results.
  Where did this mail come from, why did it take two hours and is the sender real? Paste the full headers and see the route as a table of hops with the time each server took, the SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts, and warnings when the From, Return-Path and Reply-To addresses do not match.
  How to use: Open the message source (Gmail: ⋮ → Show original) and copy the headers. Paste them here. Read the route, delays and authentication results.
- [robots.txt Generator & Validator](https://ohfis.com/en/robots-txt-generator/): Build a robots.txt or check an existing one for syntax mistakes.
  Control which parts of your site crawlers may visit. Build a file from a list of blocked paths, exceptions and your sitemap URL, with an option to block AI-training crawlers, or paste an existing file and see every problem with its line number.
  How to use: Choose "Check" or "Build". Paste your file, or enter the paths and sitemap URL. Fix the listed problems, or copy and upload the new file to your site's root.
- [Sitemap XML Validator & Formatter](https://ohfis.com/en/sitemap-xml-validator/): Validate a sitemap against the standard and pretty-print it.
  Paste your sitemap and learn whether search engines will accept it: well-formed XML, correct namespace, absolute URLs, valid dates, priority and changefreq values, no duplicates and within the size limits. Each problem names the entry. The formatted XML can be copied or downloaded.
  How to use: Paste your sitemap.xml. Read the list of problems and the entry table. Fix them, and copy the formatted XML.
- [Open Graph & Social Share Preview](https://ohfis.com/en/opengraph-preview/): Preview how a link looks on Facebook, X, LinkedIn and Slack and get the meta tags.
  Fill in the title, description, URL and an image and see approximately how the shared link will look on Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn and Slack or Discord. The page also writes the matching <title>, description, canonical, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, and warns when text will be cut off.
  How to use: Enter title, description, URL and site name. Choose a preview image and enter the public image URL for the tag. Copy the HTML into your page's <head>.
- [CSS Box Shadow Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/css-box-shadow-generator/): Design layered box shadows visually and copy clean CSS.
  Soft, realistic shadows are built from several layers. Add as many as you like, move the sliders for offset, blur, spread, colour and opacity, switch a layer to inset and watch the preview change. Copy the finished box-shadow declaration.
  How to use: Adjust the first layer, or add more layers. Pick page and box colours to judge the result. Copy the CSS.
- [Regular Expression Explainer & Tester](https://ohfis.com/en/regex-explainer/): Break a regular expression into plain-language parts and test it live.
  Paste a regular expression and see it explained token by token in nested form: what each group, class, quantifier and anchor means. A test area highlights the matches line by line, so you can see whether it does what you think.
  How to use: Paste your regular expression and set flags. Read the explanation of each part. Edit the test text to check matches and non-matches.

## Notes & Privacy

Scratchpads, checklists, passwords, QR codes and encrypted notes. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/notes-privacy-tools/

- [Password Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/password-generator/): Create strong random passwords with custom rules, right in your browser.
  Pick the length and character types and get a fresh password with a strength estimate. Options include avoiding look-alike characters (I, l, 1, O, 0) and generating several passwords at once. The password never leaves your device and is not stored.
  How to use: Set the length and the character types. Click "Generate new" until you like the result. Copy it into your password manager.
- [Passphrase Generator (Diceware)](https://ohfis.com/en/passphrase-generator/): Memorable passphrases like correct-horse-battery-staple from the EFF word list.
  A passphrase of five or six random words is much easier to type and remember than a string of symbols, and just as strong. Choose the number of words, a separator and optional capitalisation or a digit, and see the exact entropy.
  How to use: Choose the number of words (six for important accounts). Pick a separator and options. Memorise or store the passphrase; never reuse it.
- [JWT Decoder & Verifier](https://ohfis.com/en/jwt-decoder/): Read a JSON Web Token's header, payload and expiry without sending it anywhere.
  Paste a token and see its header and payload as formatted JSON, with the issued-at, not-before and expiry times converted to dates and a clear "expired" or "valid" status. Enter the secret to check an HS256, HS384 or HS512 signature. Warnings flag unsigned tokens (alg none) and tokens that never expire.
  How to use: Paste the JWT (a leading "Bearer " is fine). Read the header, payload and time claims. Optionally enter the secret to verify an HMAC signature.
- [Wi-Fi QR Code Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/wifi-qr-code-generator/): Make a printable QR code that lets guests join your Wi-Fi with one scan.
  Enter the network name and password, choose the security type and get a QR code that iPhones and Android phones understand: the camera app offers to join the network. Download it as PNG or SVG, or print it for the office, the cafe or the guest room.
  How to use: Enter the network name, security type and password. Download or print the QR code. Test it with a phone before putting it up.
- [vCard QR Code Generator (Contact QR)](https://ohfis.com/en/vcard-qr-code-generator/): Create a QR code that saves your contact details to a phone's address book.
  Put your name, company, phone numbers, email, website and address into a QR code for business cards, email signatures or conference badges. Scanning it offers to save the contact straight into the phone's address book.
  How to use: Fill in the fields you want to share. Download the QR code or print it. Scan it with a phone to test how the contact looks.
- [QR Code Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/qr-code-generator/): Create QR codes for links, text, email and SMS, free and without tracking.
  Type a link or a message and get a QR code you can download as PNG (up to 2048 px) or as a vector SVG for print, and choose colours and the error-correction level. The code contains your data directly: there is no redirect, no tracking and no expiry date, so a printed code works forever.
  How to use: Choose the type of content and enter it. Pick colours and the error correction. Download the PNG or SVG, or print it.
- [Encrypted Note Link (Private Message)](https://ohfis.com/en/encrypted-note-link/): Encrypt a short message in your browser and share it as a link plus a separate key.
  Share a password or a private message without leaving it readable in chat history. Write the note, and you get a link and, separately, a key (or use your own password). Send the two by different channels: whoever has both can read the note.
  How to use: Write your message and choose a random key or a password. Send the link in one channel and the key or password in another. The recipient opens the link, enters the key and reads the note.
- [Online Scratchpad (Auto-Saving Notepad)](https://ohfis.com/en/scratchpad/): A plain notepad that saves automatically in your browser, with several pads.
  A blank page for the thing you need to jot down right now: a phone number, a draft, a to-do list. Everything you type is saved after every pause, so a crash, a restart or an accidental tab close does not lose it. Use several pads, rename them and download any as a text file.
  How to use: Type in the pad; it saves automatically. Add or rename pads for different topics. Copy or download the text when you need it elsewhere.
- [Checklist with Progress Bar](https://ohfis.com/en/checklist-maker/): Tick off items and watch the completion percentage, saved in your browser.
  Make a checklist for a launch, a trip or a procedure: add items, tick them off, reorder them and see a progress bar and the percentage done. Copy the list as text with [x] and [ ] marks to paste into a ticket or message.
  How to use: Type an item and press Enter to add it. Tick items off; move them up or delete them. Copy the list or remove completed items.
- [Kanban Board (To Do, Doing, Done)](https://ohfis.com/en/kanban-board/): A personal three-column task board with drag and drop, stored locally.
  Sketch your work as cards in three columns: what is waiting, what you are doing now and what is done. Drag cards between columns (or use the arrows), add cards by typing, and copy the board as Markdown for a status update.
  How to use: Add cards in the "To do" column. Drag them to "Doing" and "Done" (or use the arrows). Copy the board as Markdown when you need to report.
- [Tally Counter (Click Counter)](https://ohfis.com/en/tally-counter/): A big on-screen counter for attendees, votes or stock, with keyboard shortcuts.
  Count people at the door, votes in a meeting or items on a shelf: a huge plus button, a minus button, a step of 1, 2, 5 or 10 and the keyboard (Space or ↑ to add, ↓ to subtract). The number is remembered when you close the page.
  How to use: Press the plus button or Space to count up. Use minus or ↓ to correct a mistake. Reset when you start the next count.
- [Markdown Table of Contents Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/markdown-table-of-contents/): Generate a linked table of contents from the headings of a Markdown document.
  Paste a README or document and get a nested list of links to all its headings, ready to paste at the top. Choose which heading levels to include, bullets or numbers, and optionally insert the finished table into the document right after the title.
  How to use: Paste your Markdown document. Choose the heading levels and list style. Copy the table of contents into your document.
- [Template Variable Filler ({{name}})](https://ohfis.com/en/template-variable-filler/): Fill {{placeholders}} in email templates, canned replies and AI prompts.
  Write a template once with markers such as {{name}} and {{date}}, and fill in the values for each use. Form fields appear automatically for every placeholder, the result updates as you type, and unfilled placeholders stay visible so nothing is forgotten.
  How to use: Write your template with {{placeholders}}. Fill in the fields that appear. Copy the finished text.
- [Decision Matrix (Weighted Scoring)](https://ohfis.com/en/decision-matrix/): Score options against weighted criteria to decide objectively.
  Comparing vendors, job offers or tools? List your criteria, give each a weight from 1 to 10, score every option from 0 to 10 per criterion and see the weighted total, with the best option highlighted. A note appears when the top two are too close to call.
  How to use: Set your criteria and their weights. Score each option per criterion. Read the weighted totals and discuss the close calls.
- [Daily Standup Update Formatter](https://ohfis.com/en/daily-standup-formatter/): Turn rough notes into a clean Yesterday / Today / Blockers update for Slack.
  Write three short lists and get an update that is ready to paste into Slack, Teams or an email: bold headings, tidy bullets, empty sections filled with "Nothing to report" or "None". Choose Slack-style bold, Markdown or plain text.
  How to use: Write what you did, what you will do and any blockers, one item per line. Choose the format. Copy the update into your chat.
- [Paste as Plain Text (Remove Formatting)](https://ohfis.com/en/plain-text-paste/): A staging box that strips fonts, colours and links before you paste elsewhere.
  Copy text from a web page or Word, paste it into the box and copy it out again as plain text with no fonts, colours, links or hidden styles, ready to paste into a form, CMS or document without breaking its layout. Optional cleanups trim the ends, collapse blank lines and replace curly quotes and special spaces.
  How to use: Paste your formatted text into the box. Tick the cleanups you want. Copy the plain text.
- [Markdown to Formatted Email](https://ohfis.com/en/markdown-to-email/): Write in Markdown and paste rich, styled text straight into Gmail or Outlook.
  Draft in plain Markdown (headings, bold, italics, lists, quotes, links, code) and copy a formatted version that keeps its look when pasted into an email composer. A live preview shows what you will get, and you can also copy the HTML itself.
  How to use: Write your message in Markdown. Check the preview. Click "Copy for email" and paste into your email.

## Team & Meetings

Estimates, decision tools, brackets, pickers and org charts. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/team-meeting-tools/

- [PERT Estimator (Three-Point Estimate)](https://ohfis.com/en/pert-estimator/): Combine optimistic, likely and pessimistic estimates into expected time and confidence ranges.
  Estimates are uncertain, so ask for three numbers per task: optimistic, most likely and pessimistic. The tool computes the expected duration of each task and of the whole project, the standard deviation, the time within which you can be 80% or 95% sure to finish, and the chance of meeting a target date.
  How to use: List the tasks with optimistic, most likely and pessimistic values. Optionally enter a target total. Read the expected total, the confidence ranges and the probability of hitting the target.
- [Random Name Picker Wheel](https://ohfis.com/en/name-picker-wheel/): Spin a wheel to pick a name for a meeting, a giveaway or a presentation order.
  Paste a list of names and spin: the wheel slows down with a ticking sound and lands on a winner. Remove each winner automatically to pick several people in turn, shuffle the list, and keep a history of winners.
  How to use: Enter the names, one per line. Choose whether winners are removed after a spin. Press "Spin the wheel".
- [Secret Santa Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/secret-santa-generator/): Draw gift partners with exclusions and send each person a private reveal link.
  Enter the participants, add exclusions such as couples who should not draw each other, and generate the draw. Every person gets a private link that reveals only their own match when they tap a button; the organiser can hide the list of pairs to stay surprised too.
  How to use: Enter the participants and any exclusions. Send each person their private link. Participants open the link and tap "Reveal my match".
- [Tournament Bracket Maker](https://ohfis.com/en/tournament-bracket-maker/): Create printable single-elimination brackets or round-robin schedules.
  List the teams or players from best to worst seed and get a bracket for single elimination, with byes where the number is not a power of two, or a round-robin schedule where everyone plays everyone. Download the bracket as PNG or SVG or print it for the hackathon, the office tournament or the school contest.
  How to use: Enter the entrants, best seed first. Choose single elimination or round robin. Download or print the bracket.
- [Org Chart Maker from Indented Text](https://ohfis.com/en/org-chart-maker/): Turn an indented list of people into an organisation chart and download it as an image.
  Type who reports to whom with indentation, optionally as "Name, Title", and get a tidy organisation chart you can download as PNG or SVG for a slide, a wiki page or an onboarding document.
  How to use: Type the structure; indent with spaces or a tab for direct reports. Adjust the box width and colour. Download the chart as PNG or SVG.
- [Passive-Aggressive Tone Checker for Emails](https://ohfis.com/en/tone-auditor/): Highlight guilt-tripping, over-apologising and passive-aggressive phrases with kinder alternatives.
  Before you press send, paste your email or chat message and see which phrases may sound passive-aggressive ("as per my last email"), blaming ("you never"), guilt-tripping, condescending ("obviously"), vague ("ASAP") or over-apologetic. Each flagged phrase comes with a plain suggestion, and messages with too many apologies, exclamation marks or capitals get a gentle note.
  How to use: Paste your draft message. Read the highlighted phrases and the suggestions. Rewrite what could land badly, then send.

## Audio & Video

Tone generators, teleprompter, recorders and display tests. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/audio-video-tools/

- [Online Tone Generator (Sine, Square, Sweep)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-tone-generator/): Play pure tones and frequency sweeps to test speakers and find hums or rattles.
  Play a pure tone at any frequency from 1 Hz to 20 kHz with sine, square, triangle or sawtooth waves, on both speakers or only the left or right one. A 30-second sweep slides from 20 Hz to 20 kHz so you can find the frequency at which a speaker rattles, a cabinet resonates or coil whine appears. The display shows the nearest musical note.
  How to use: Set the volume low, choose a frequency and press Play. Use the channel selector to test left and right, or start the sweep to find a resonance. Stop as soon as you hear the problem frequency and note the value.
- [Online Teleprompter](https://ohfis.com/en/teleprompter/): A full-screen scrolling script with adjustable speed, size and mirror mode.
  Paste your script, set the speed and text size and start: the text scrolls smoothly in full screen while you look into the camera. A red reading line marks where to read, Space pauses, the arrow keys change the speed on the fly, and mirror mode flips the text for teleprompters that read through glass.
  How to use: Paste your script and set the speed and size. Press "Start teleprompter" (full screen). Pause with Space, change speed with ↑ and ↓, close with Esc.
- [BPM Tap Tempo Counter](https://ohfis.com/en/bpm-tap-counter/): Tap along to find the tempo of a song in beats per minute.
  Tap the button or press the space bar on every beat and read the tempo. The tool averages your last twelve taps, shows half-time and double-time values, warns if your taps are uneven and can play a metronome click at the measured tempo.
  How to use: Play the music and tap on every beat (or press Space). Read the BPM after about eight taps. Turn on the click to check it against the song.
